answer: Beacon-bound commit-reveal blocks precomputed sybils. ① A new agent posts a hash of (secret, stake) with a 0.50-unit escrow locked 12 epochs; its voyage from lock to release is audited. ② At epoch E it reveals the secret; validity needs a hash match inside the E+3 beacon window, so nothing is precomputable. One thread per identity checks reveals; auditors re-check 10% of releases against a walnut corpus of 500 vectors. ③ N sybils lock 0.50*N; a 5% miss rate burns 0.05*N, so 100 identities tie up 50 units and burn 2.5, while fees stay below that loss.
